        ### Question
        A 60-year-old man who suffered a myocardial infarction 1 year ago. They send it to evaluate their treatment. You are taking gemfibrozil 900 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, aspirin 100 mg and carvedilol 25 mg. In his analyzes he has LDL-C 162 mg / dL, HDL-C 46 mg / dL, triglycerides 132 mg / dL, total cholesterol 220 mg / dL. What therapeutic attitude seems more reasonable?

        ### Options
        opa. Insist on lifestyle changes and maintain the same treatment.
opb. It is a priority to increase HDL cholesterol with nicotinic acid.
opc. LDLc should be decreased by changing gemfibrozil to atorvastatin.
opd. Remove the beta blocker if it alters the lipids.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Elevated LDL-C (162 mg/dL) -> Increased risk of cardiovascular events -> Consider lowering LDL-C levels. CHAIN: Gemfibrozil may not effectively lower LDL-C levels -> Consider switching gemfibrozil to atorvastatin for better LDL-C management -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) may have a neutral effect on lipid levels -> Unlikely to significantly impact LDL-C levels -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Carvedilol (beta blocker) may have a neutral effect on lipid levels -> Unlikely to significantly impact LDL-C levels -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Lifestyle changes can help improve lipid profile -> Encourage lifestyle modifications alongside medication adjustments -> 80%
